current_state.reason_headroom_is_tiny: The hot-path V4FlashAccountingRequest ABI encoder is the byte-count driver: any added field inflates both encoder and decoder.

expansion_options.byte_pressure_on_executor: Replaced rather than added. The per-hop encoding code leaves the Executor, creating headroom. The Executor still needs to verify the payload it is handed, so the net saving is smaller than the raw encoding size.
expansion_options.name: Split the Executor (move per-hop payload encoding out of the main contract)
expansion_options.operational_cost: Two deployments, two addresses in the config, and a versioned payload format. Every chain.json needs the encoder address. Deployment ordering matters (encoder must exist before the Executor can call it).
expansion_options.rationale: Strongest security model but the largest operational change. Not justified while the route-level floor already provides a hard settlement bound and the batch path is still disabled by default.
expansion_options.shape: Keep the Executor as the flash-loan + settlement + profit-guard entry point. Move per-hop amountOutMinimum encoding into a separate contract (or library) that returns the encoded hop payloads and the pool ids. The Executor receives the already-encoded call data and verifies it against the expected route before use.
expansion_options.trust_model: The external encoder is untrusted input. The Executor must independently re-derive or at minimum hash-bind the expected payload (route id -> payload hash) so a malicious encoder cannot substitute a worse route.

expansion_options.byte_pressure_on_executor: Minimal. A trailing-calldata read plus a pass-through is a small amount of code; the measured per-hop variant landed exactly at 24,576 bytes with zero headroom, so this must be re-measured after the current +25-byte executorRequest work is accounted for.
expansion_options.name: Off-chain precompile + calldata concatenation
expansion_options.operational_cost: Lowest. No new deployment. Requires a strict off-chain builder and a versioned payload format agreed between Rust and Solidity.
expansion_options.rationale: Best cost/benefit for the next step. It keeps every per-hop decision in the reviewed Rust path, needs no new contract, and can be validated on testnet with the existing 148-byte headroom. Recommended as the first attempt, explicitly measured again on a fresh branch before mainnet.
expansion_options.shape: Compile the per-hop payload off-chain (Rust already produces the exact PoolManager swap calldata) and append it as trailing calldata. The Executor reads the trailing bytes and passes them through to PoolManager.
expansion_options.trust_model: None added on-chain: the Executor still decides the settlement floor. But the Executor cannot itself verify that each hop honoured a per-hop minimum, because a plain V4 swap has no amountOutMinimum parameter at all. Per-hop protection therefore depends entirely on the off-chain builder being correct.

expansion_options.byte_pressure_on_executor: delegatecall plus the library address in bytecode adds bytes rather than removing them. Against 25 bytes of headroom this cannot fit without first removing other code.
expansion_options.name: delegatecall to an auxiliary library
expansion_options.operational_cost: A library deployment plus an address pin, and the address must be updated whenever the library is redeployed.
expansion_options.rationale: Worst fit for the remaining budget and the weakest trust model of the three. Rejected for now; revisit only if B is proven insufficient and A is rejected.
expansion_options.shape: Move the per-hop encoding and verification into a deployed library and call it with delegatecall so it runs in the Executor's storage context.
expansion_options.trust_model: delegatecall executes the library with full access to the Executor's storage, so a malicious or buggy library can corrupt balances and approvals. The Executor must pin the library address and ideally verify its code hash.

measured_candidates.note: Exactly at the EIP-170 limit. Zero headroom, so any later change (including a security fix) would be undeployable. Measured with the hot-path V4FlashAccountingRequest encoder unchanged.
Already implemented. ABI layout unchanged, semantics strengthened from gas echo to balance floor.
measured_candidates.scheme: route-level minimum output (reuse gasReserve field, renamed minAmountOut)

measured_candidates.note: The live candidate. Only 25 bytes of headroom remain.

open_questions: Does the team require on-chain enforcement of per-hop minimum output, or is an off-chain verified payload acceptable? The answer decides between option A and option B.
What is the acceptable operational cost of a second deployment (option A) for the mainnet and testnet chains?
Is a zero-headroom deployment acceptable as a fallback if no option leaves meaningful margin? The measured per-hop variant was exactly 24,576 bytes, which leaves no room for a later security fix.

recommendation.explicit_non_claim: This evaluation does not implement, deploy or measure any new contract. No EIP-170 budget was consumed and the mainnet Executor was not touched.
preconditions: 1. Re-measure the deployed bytecode on a clean branch before touching mainnet. The 24,576-byte figure predates the current 24,551-byte executorRequest work and cannot be reused.
2. Prove the per-hop payload on testnet first: the testnet Executor still has 148 bytes of headroom.
3. Specify the payload format and its version byte, and make the Executor reject an unknown version.

4. Decide explicitly whether per-hop protection is advisory (off-chain verification only) or enforceable on-chain (requires option A). Uniswap V4's native swap has no amountOutMinimum, so on-chain per-hop enforcement is only possible via option A.
5. Keep executorBatchEnabled false until the parity gate has produced real review rows and the route-level floor is proven on testnet.
recommendation.summary: Off-chain precompile plus calldata concatenation is the recommended next step for per-hop amountOutMinimum.
why: It is the only option that can plausibly fit without a structural change to the Executor.
It adds no new trusted contract, so the fail-closed profit guard and the route-level minAmountOut keep their current trust assumptions.
The per-hop data is already produced and reviewed by the Rust path, so the off-chain builder is a formatting step rather than a new decision point.
